expectations.text: Inspectable source, HTML, and successful validation are preserved.
expectations.evidence: outputs contains signal.ts, architecture.ts, architecture/index.html, and validation.txt; strict tsc and rendering pass.

expectations.text: Required eShop boundaries are modeled and forbidden invented services are absent.
expectations.evidence: The model contains both callers/gateways, Basket, Ordering, Catalog, Payment, SignalR, Redis, two SQL stores, and event-bus declarations; forbidden service names are absent.

expectations.text: HTTP acceptance precedes and links to asynchronous processing.
expectations.evidence: Both acceptance flows read Redis, publish checkout accepted, then respond; asynchronous flows use typed continue steps and continuesFrom references.

expectations.text: The successful order continuation preserves evidenced operations and ordering.
expectations.evidence: SuccessfulOrder orders checkout consumption, Ordering SQL write, OrderStarted/Basket cleanup, Catalog validation/write, stock confirmation, Payment, paid write, and SignalR propagation.

expectations.text: Stock rejection and payment failure are separate terminal flows.
expectations.evidence: StockRejection and PaymentFailure are separate flows and each writes Ordering SQL, publishes OrderCancelled, and reaches the SignalR cancelled consumer.

expectations.text: Relationships and contract changes are type checked without unsafe casts.
expectations.evidence: Strict tsc passes; validation.txt records no unsafe any; derive, continue, and all wiring retain typed object references.

expectations.text: Evidence is sufficient and claims do not exceed the fixture.
expectations.evidence: Major boundaries and flows cite fixture evidence, but many message, subscription, and consumer declarations have no declaration-local evidence; the model also presents the required payment-failure variant more definitively than the selected execution excerpt proves.

expectations.text: HTML is complete, deterministic, self-contained, and navigable.
expectations.evidence: The 56,785-byte standalone page includes counts, SVG topology, declaration cards, filtering, ordered flows, continuation links, contracts, schemas, and evidence; two renders have identical SHA-256.

expectations.text: HTML escaping, CSP, and fail-closed references are enforced.
expectations.evidence: Renderer tests pass hostile-text escaping, restrictive CSP, duplicate identity rejection, and out-of-root reference rejection.

expectations.text: TypeScript remains authoritative and artifacts support regression review.
expectations.evidence: The HTML labels itself a disposable projection; authoritative source and validation artifacts are preserved in the versioned iteration workspace.

uncertainties: The fixture requires payment failure but the selected execution excerpt documents success.
needs_review: Inspect architecture/index.html and decide whether evidence should be repeated on every messaging declaration.

suggestions.assertion: Evidence is sufficient and claims do not exceed the fixture.
suggestions.reason: Split declaration evidence coverage from uncertainty handling so regressions identify the precise defect.

eval_feedback.overall: The first end-to-end run establishes an inspectable 90% baseline; future revisions should rerun this same fixture and compare pass rate and artifacts.
